newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: ENDEMOL SHARES TO BE OFFERED AT 44-48 GUILDERS.
newsitem.headline: ENDEMOL SHARES TO BE OFFERED AT 44-48 GUILDERS.

text.p: Shares of television producer and entertainment group Endemol Entertainment Holding NV will be offered at a price of between 44 and 48 guilders, ABN AMRO Bank said on Thursday.
The transaction is a primary and secondary offering up too 9,688,800 ordinary Endemol shares.
For the offering a book-building system will be used, in which institutional investors can indicate the number of shares they want to buy and at what price.
ABN AMRO said it expects the price to be announced on Thursday, November 7, when the shares will be allocated. Payment and delivery are expected on November 12.
The subscription opens on October 25 and is expected to close on November 6 at 1500 hrs local Dutch time (1400 GMT).
The subscription period can be closed earlier or later, ABN AMRO said in a statement.
Endemol intends to issue up to 4.40 million new shares for the flotation which will increase its number of outstanding shares by 15 percent.
Current shareholders will offer up to 5.28 million existing shares, representing 18 percent of the share capital.

ABN AMRO said the selling shareholders have granted ABN AMRO Rothschild, on behalf of the issuing syndicate, an option to buy an additional 1.45 million Endemol shares which can be exercised within 30 days after the offering closes.
The Endemol shares are expected to start trading on the Amsterdam Stock Exchange on November 7.
Endemol previously announced it was seeking a partial flotation of its shares to finance foreign expansion.

The group, formed in 1994 when the production companies of co-chairmen Joop van den Ende and John de Mol merged, already generates about 40 percent of its television programming turnover outside the Netherlands. Television programming brings in just under 80 percent of Endemol's turnover with the rest generated by its live entertainment division.
Endemol's net profit rose by more than 38 percent to 60.5 million guilders in the financial year to July 31, 1996 on a turnover of 642.4 million guilders.
The company expected net profits to rise by 15 to 20 percent in the current 1996/97 financial year and previously said it saw both sales and profits doubling within five years.
